title: English File Intermediate, File 4: have to, must, should; can, could, be able to

fixIt.text: You haven't to wear a uniform at our office.
fixIt.explain: No need: don't have to + verb.

fixIt.text: She has to working on Saturdays.
You should calling your mother more often.
Do we must bring our passports?
fixIt.explain: Questions about rules: Do we have to …?

fixIt.text: Students mustn't using phones during the exam.
fixIt.explain: mustn't + verb: it is not allowed.

fixIt.text: I will can drive next year.
fixIt.explain: can has no future form: will be able to.

fixIt.text: When I was a child, I can swim very well.
She hasn't could find a job yet.
fixIt.explain: can has no perfect form: hasn't been able to.

fixIt.text: Were you able finish the report?
The lesson was so bored that I fell asleep.
fixIt.explain: The lesson was boring; I was bored.

fixIt.text: We were really exciting about the trip to Japan.
fixIt.explain: How you feel: -ed (excited); the trip is exciting.

builder.tip: don't have to = it's not necessary.

builder.text: I couldn't swim when I was young.
alternatives: When I was young I couldn't swim.

builder.text: She was bored at the party.

radio.title: Phones at work
radio.text: At my office, there are a few rules about phones. We don't have to turn them off, but we must put them on silent during meetings. You shouldn't answer personal calls at your desk, because it disturbs other people. Last week a new colleague couldn't find the meeting room, so she called me. I was able to help her, but my manager was annoyed because my phone rang in the middle of his presentation. It was really embarrassing.
